tier_reason: Peer-reviewed paper (The BLAS API of BLASFEO, arXiv 1902.08115) benchmarks single-threaded BLASFEO vs OpenBLAS 0.3.4-dev, BLIS 0.5.0 and MKL 2019.1 on named CPUs; compiler and flags are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 2-3x faster than OpenBLAS and BLIS for level-3 BLAS at matrix sizes in the tens on Haswell, ~2x for LAPACK factorizations up to size 100; competitive with MKL on dgemm and faster than MKL on other level-3 and LAPACK routines; ~2x on Cortex A57, larger margin on Cortex A53
corrections.compiler_and_flags: not stated in paper (libraries single-threaded; MKL with MKL_DIRECT_CALL_SEQ)
corrections.caveats: Paper numbers from 2019-2020 (OpenBLAS 0.3.4-dev, BLIS 0.5.0, MKL 2019.1); single-threaded only; win is for small cache-resident matrices, not large ones; compiler/flags not stated

notes: Paper gives 'factor 2 or 3' for sizes in the tens, not 1.5-3x up to 100; corrected. Metadata (BSD-2-Clause, 415 stars, last commit 2026-09-29) checks out.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed IWOCL '18 paper compares CLBlast 1.3.0 GEMM against clBLAS 2.12 on 7 devices and shows it significantly better overall, but gives the win qualitatively and in graphs, without a numeric ratio vs clBLAS; tier B stays, the claim was overstated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Significantly better overall GEMM performance than clBLAS 2.12, especially for irregular sizes (multiples of 129) and on Skylake/NVIDIA (graphs only, no numeric ratio in text); cuBLAS remains faster than CLBlast
corrections.baseline: clBLAS 2.12 (cuBLAS also tested; it is faster)
corrections.caveats: Baselines are GPU BLAS libraries, not OpenBLAS/MKL/Eigen/BLIS; NVIDIA cuBLAS beats CLBlast in the paper; the ~2x FP16 figure is vs CLBlast's own FP32 and the up-to-10x batched figure is vs non-batched calls, neither is vs a baseline library; versions <=1.6.2 had correctness issues on Intel Arc A770 and other devices (fixed in 1.6.3)

notes: Record said 'approaching cuBLAS' but the paper says cuBLAS is still superior; the 2x/10x numbers are self-comparisons. Metadata (Apache-2.0, 1.2k stars, last commit 2026-09-28) checks out.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed ICS '21 paper reports up to 22.14% over OpenBLAS, 21.70% over BLIS and 3.50% over MKL on Skylake Gold 5122 / Cascade Lake W-2255 with icc 19.0 -O3; the code is now public but no benchmark harness was confirmed in it, so not A.

corrections.caveats: Gains are 'up to' figures from the paper; code was released later at github.com/yzhaiustc/ftblas (GPL-3.0, linked from ftblas.org), mainly double precision; last commit 2023-02-28; the benchmark harness for the paper's numbers was not confirmed in the repo

notes: The code was released after the paper: set repo_url to https://github.com/yzhaiustc/ftblas (repo_url is not a correction field; repo language not checked). The ICS'21 numbers match the record.
